items.informal_name: Cardinality of Image of Injective Binary Function on Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ},
  Function.Injective2 f → ∀ (s : Finset α) (t : Finset β), (Finset.image₂ f s t).card = s.card * t.card
items.informal_description: If $ f : \alpha \times \beta \to \gamma $ is an injective binary function, then for any finite sets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $, the cardinality of the image $ \{ f(a, b) \mid a \in s, b \in t \} $ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of $ s $ and $ t $, i.e., $ |\text{image}_2(f, s, t)| = |s| \cdot |t| $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Binary Image Equals Product iff Injective on Cartesian Product
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β},
  (Finset.image₂ f s t).card = s.card * t.card ↔ Set.InjOn (fun x => f x.1 x.2) (↑s ×ˢ ↑t)
items.informal_description: The cardinality of the image of a binary function $ f $ on finite sets $ s $ and $ t $ equals the product $ \#s \cdot \#t $ if and only if $ f $ is injective on the Cartesian product $ s \times t $. In symbols, $ \#(\mathrm{image}_2\, f\, s\, t) = \#s \cdot \#t $ if and only if $ (s \times t).\mathrm{InjOn}\, (\lambda (a,b), f(a,b)) $. This characterizes when the binary function preserves distinctness across all pairs in the Cartesian product.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Binary Image with Singleton Second Set Under Injectivity
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} (s : Finset α) {b : β},
  (Function.Injective fun a => f a b) → (Finset.image₂ f s {b}).card = s.card
items.informal_description: If the function $ f $ is injective in its first argument when the second argument is fixed to $ b $, then the cardinality of the image of $ f $ over the finite set $ s $ and the singleton set $ \{b\} $ is equal to the cardinality of $ s $, i.e., $ \#\{f(a, b) \mid a \in s\} = \#s $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality Inequality for Binary Function Image with Injective First Argument
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} (s : Finset α) {b : β}
  {t : Finset β}, b ∈ t → (Function.Injective fun x => f x b) → s.card ≤ (Finset.image₂ f s t).card
items.informal_description: Let $ s $ be a finite set over $ \alpha $, $ t $ a finite set over $ \beta $, and $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $ a binary function. If there exists an element $ b \in t $ such that the function $ f(\cdot, b) : \alpha \to \gamma $ is injective, then the cardinality of $ s $ is less than or equal to the cardinality of the image of $ f $ applied to all pairs $ (a, b') $ with $ a \in s $ and $ b' \in t $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Binary Image with Left Singleton and Injective Function
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} (t : Finset β) {a : α},
  Function.Injective (f a) → (Finset.image₂ f {a} t).card = t.card
items.informal_description: For a binary function $ f $, an element $ a $, and a finite set $ t $, if the function $ f(a, \cdot) $ is injective, then the cardinality of the image of $ f $ applied to the singleton set $ \{a\} $ and $ t $ is equal to the cardinality of $ t $, i.e., $ \# \text{image}_2(f, \{a\}, t) = \# t $.
